philosophy.title: Fluency = Speaking Confidently with Real People
philosophy.body: Fluency isn't perfection — it's the confidence to open your mouth with a real Portuguese person and keep going. Every feature here (role-plays, speaking practice, missions) aims at that one goal.

philosophy.title: Train, Don't Study
philosophy.body: Speaking is a physical skill, like futebol or surfing. Reading about Portuguese doesn't build it; repeating real phrases out loud every day does. 10 minutes daily beats 2 hours on Sunday.

philosophy.title: Mistakes Are the Method
philosophy.body: The Portuguese are genuinely kind with learners — one honest attempt at 'obrigado' earns real warmth. Make mistakes fast, get corrected, move on.

philosophy.title: Don't Translate in Your Head
philosophy.body: Attach Portuguese phrases directly to situations and feelings. 'Tudo bem?' isn't 'is everything good?' — it's what you say when you see someone. That's why every lesson is a situation, not a word list.

philosophy.title: Use It or Lose It
philosophy.body: You remember 'se faz favor' because you'd actually say it. The spaced-repetition deck exists for the same reason: phrases reviewed on schedule become phrases you own.

trainingSteps.title: Listen & Imitate (Shadowing)
trainingSteps.body: Play the line audio and imitate it exactly — European Portuguese is fast and swallows vowels. Copy the rhythm and the swallowed endings, not just the words.

trainingSteps.title: Read the Dialogue
trainingSteps.body: Open the lesson and read both sides of the conversation. Understand the situation first — a pastelaria, a farmácia, a grelhada — then the lines.

trainingSteps.title: Role-Play Both Sides
trainingSteps.body: Run the interactive role-play. Play yourself first, then play the Portuguese partner. Speaking the other side doubles your listening comprehension.

trainingSteps.title: Speak It & Get Scored
trainingSteps.body: Use Speaking Practice: say each line out loud until the tutor hears a clean match. If the app can't understand you, a Lisboeta will struggle too — that's the point of the test.

trainingSteps.title: Take It to the Street
trainingSteps.body: Finish the lesson quiz, then do the real-world version: order the bica, ask the question, send the voice message. Real use is the final rep.

mindset.title: The Portuguese appreciate effort
mindset.body: Portugal is modest but warm: try two words of Portuguese and doors open. Your accent is a conversation starter, not a problem.

mindset.title: Reply in Portuguese, not English
mindset.body: Many Portuguese speak excellent English and will switch — politely stay in Portuguese anyway: 'Posso praticar?'. That sentence is a superpower.

mindset.title: Learn the rhythm first
mindset.body: European Portuguese swallows unstressed vowels. If your 'obrigado' sounds like 'brigadu', you're on the right track — that's how it really sounds.

mindset.title: Ask like a child
mindset.body: 'O que significa isto?' — children ask endlessly and learn endlessly. Curiosity beats embarrassment.

mindset.title: Don't fear the guttural R
mindset.body: The throat R (rua, carro) feels strange for two weeks and natural forever after. Just do it badly until you do it well.

mindset.title: Have a purpose
mindset.body: Your goals — traveling Portugal, talking to Portuguese friends or family, understanding fado — are the fuel. Revisit them when motivation dips.

mindset.title: Telenovelas are training
mindset.body: Series and music aren't a break from studying — they ARE studying, if you log what you catch in the tracker.

mindset.title: A little slang goes far
mindset.body: One well-timed 'fixe!' or 'pá' makes you instantly more local. Sprinkle, don't pour.
